newsitem.title: CHINA: China moves to curb petrochemical explosions.
newsitem.headline: China moves to curb petrochemical explosions.

text.p: China's Fire Fighting Bureau has ordered a safety campaign in the petrochemical industry after a spate of deadly explosions, the Procuratorial Daily said on Tuesday.
Accidents involving petrochemicals since June had caused severe losses and damaged social stability and public order, it said.
The bureau under the Ministry of Public Security had ordered authorities nationwide to take immediate steps to improve safety in the petrochemical industry and in handling of flammable materials.
An oil tanker exploded at the Qixia anchorage in the inland port of Nanjing on June 4 killing five people, injuring five and leaving four missing.

A further eight people had been killed and 64 injured in an explosion at the Dongfang Chemical Factory in a Beijing suburb on June 27 and a blast at another Beijing chemical company on July 14 had killed one person and another injured another, the newspaper said.
On July 20, an oil tanker exploded in Hubei province killing two crew members and injuring one, it said.
A freight train carrying oil had caught fire in central Henan province on August 1, suspending all rail traffic on the line for 14 hours, it said.
The accidents showed petrochemical enterprises were neglecting fire safety precautions and breaking safety regulations, it quoted the bureau as saying.
